body: This is correct, and applies to sinumerik only and not other posts as the Sinumerik controller have its own extended standards of g-codes.
Correction to the review above: note 2 is wrong. The PR body does carry a `Changelog:` line. Nothing is missing, and the verdict stands: ready for the maintainer to merge.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 26e8610e5a6cbc7feb4ff5c88e717d782f502b75 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** (Maintainer-side review at the high tier, since this changes posted G-code.)

Reviewed at the trial merge with current `origin/main` (9032da34). The merge was clean, including `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps` after today's hop-law and probe merges.

### What looks good
- Every place the script writes or reads a work-offset word now goes through `frameWord` / `frameOf`. I grepped `sinumerik.cps` for `G5`, `wcs`, `WorkOffset` and `UIFR`. The only writers of the word are the section opening block (`block(["G17","G710","G90",wcsWord,...])`, l.355) and the probe re-select (l.668). Both read `wcsWord`, which is now set only through `frameWord` in `onParameter` (l.302). The `OPERATION:` comment (l.207) prints the mapped word. The retracts use `G53`, which is not a frame word. Tilt is refused outright (`tiltOk`), so there is no CYCLE800 or TRANS/ROT path that could re-select a frame.
- The offset still comes from the setup only (`posting::wcs_context` -> `WCS_SLOTS[slot]`). The post maps that word and derives nothing.
- Probe indices are right: G54..G57 -> `$P_UIFR[1..4]`, G505 -> 5, G506 -> 6 (`frameOf`). Setting offset 6 from G54 posts `$P_UIFR[6,X,TR]=$P_UIFR[1,X,TR]+R90`, which is pinned.
- A word that names no settable frame (e.g. `G53`) is refused by name with a counted warning, so the post is blocked. A probe `SetWorkOffset` past offset 6 (`G60`..) is refused twice (by `frameWord` and by the existing `!to` check) and writes nothing.
- The new test fails without the fix. I reverted the `onParameter` line locally and got `left: ["G54","G55","G56","G57","G58","G59"]`, so both tests went red. I restored the line afterwards and did not commit it.
- Offsets 1-4 post byte-identically: the PR changes no golden, and every Sinumerik golden still passes (`conformance`, `script_sinumerik`, the recorded suites).
- Two sections on offsets 4 then 5 write `G57`, then `G505`, at each section open. This is pinned by `sinumerik_posts_offsets_one_to_six_as_their_settable_frames`.
- Clean-room: the mapping cites the public 840D sl Fundamentals and is written as our own logic. It has a provenance line, a decision file, `Changelog:` and `Fixes #934`.

### Local results (merged with main)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (22 binaries incl. `script_sinumerik`, recorded, `cycle_hop`) | 184 passed, 0 failed |
| app: `sinumerik_work_offsets` 2, `probe_dialects` 13, `conformance` 6, `sinumerik_safe_retract` 3, `program_entry` 9, `inverted_post` 15, `fanuc_post` 11, `arc_planes` 8, `wear_comp` 5, `control_comp` 5, `post_unit_word` 5, `program_comments` 4, `comment_escape` 3, `vertical_arc_entry` 3, `probe_spindle` 2, `probe_spindle_stop` 2 | all pass |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. The decision file and the PR text say a probe setting offset 6 "re-selects G506". The script re-selects the section's own frame (`block([wcsWord])`, l.668). When the probe runs in G54 and sets frame 6, the block written is `G54`, not `G506`. That is the right behaviour, because the program keeps running in its own frame, but the sentence overstates it. A one-word fix in the decision file would do.
2. The probe refusal for a `SetWorkOffset` past 6 lost its pin in the second commit ("unreachable slot-10"). The code path is still correct by reading. If the probe command really validates the slot at creation, a pointer to that validation in the commit or the decision would close the loop.
3. This existed before the PR: `frameOf` strips non-digits, so a word like `G59.5` would read as frame 95. Nothing in the engine produces such a word today. Mention only.

### Only a real control can prove
That G505/G506 select settable frames 5/6 on the target machine depends on that machine's configured frame count (MD 18601 `MM_NUM_GLOBAL_USER_FRAMES` / `MM_NUM_USER_FRAMES`). A control set up with only 4 settable frames alarms on G505. That is a safe failure (an alarm, not wrong motion), but worth a line in the machine docs.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
